opportunity.title: Survey-Based Research Platform and Platform Management Tool (RFI)
opportunity.description: The VA Acquisition Academy needs a Software as a Service survey-based research platform and platform management tool to securely collect responses to a competency survey it is piloting for acquisition human capital planning. Required: software subscriptions, maintenance and support. Period of performance is a 12-month base plus four 12-month options. Respondents provide a rough order of magnitude price against the salient characteristics by email by Oct 20, 2026.

profile._note: FICTIONAL SAMPLE COMPANY for scenario testing. Not a real firm. Past performance and staffing are invented; only the NAICS codes, set-aside definitions and every opportunity and award figure used against it are real public data.
profile.name: Cascade HUBZone Software Co. (sample)
profile.pastPerformance: HUBZone-certified in rural Oregon. One VA medical-center scheduling tool (about $400K), one county health records integration ($300K).
profile.capacityNotes: Nine staff, all in the HUBZone. No clearance. Small, focused on clinical scheduling software.
verification: NAICS codes confirmed against USAspending reference (api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/references/naics) on 2026-10-16.
Set-asides follow SBA definitions: SBA = small business, 8A = 8(a) Business Development, HUBZONE, WOSB/EDWOSB, SDVOSB.

checks.reason: Full and open competition; no set-aside required.
NAICS 541519 is in the company's codes.

rationale.point: The RFI is for a SaaS survey-based research platform and platform management tool (Claim #1), which aligns with the company's software development capabilities but is outside its core clinical scheduling domain.

The RFI requires software subscriptions, maintenance, and support (Claim #2), which the company could potentially provide given its past performance in software delivery, though at a smaller scale ($400K VA scheduling tool).

risks: Potential follow-on contract size (median top awards ~$99.5M) far exceeds company capacity (9 staff, $700K past performance).
No direct experience with survey-based research platforms; core expertise is clinical scheduling.
No security clearances; VA work may require them.
Set-aside is NONE, so HUBZone certification does not confer competitive advantage for this RFI.
nextSteps: Evaluate teaming with a larger prime that has survey research platform experience.
Assess RFI response effort vs. strategic value for future VA opportunities.
Monitor for follow-on RFP with small-business set-aside where HUBZone status would be advantageous.
